issues.title: 增加个 people 字段后，显示总是出错，希望获得您的帮助
issues.body:
编辑 schema.md 如下，企图增加一个 people 分类，但总是出现各种错误，不知道是配置的不够，还是有错误，求高手指点，先多谢！

| Type | Directory | Purpose |
|------|-----------|---------|
| entity | wiki/entities/ | Named things (tools, organizations, datasets,Excluding people) |
| ---> people | wiki/people | Names and positions of the people，Only including people |
| concept | wiki/concepts/ | Ideas, techniques, phenomena, frameworks |
| source | wiki/sources/ | Papers, articles, talks, books, blog posts |
| query | wiki/queries/ | Open questions under active investigation |
| comparison | wiki/comparisons/ | Side-by-side analysis of related entities |
| synthesis | wiki/synthesis/ | Cross-cutting summaries and conclusions |
| overview | wiki/ | High-level project summary (one per project) |

## Naming Conventions

- Files: `kebab-case.md`
- Entities: match official name where possible (e.g., `openai.md`, `gpt-4.md`)
- ---> People: match official name where possible (e.g., `刘备.md`, `张飞.md`)
- Concepts: descriptive noun phrases (e.g., `chain-of-thought.md`)
- Sources: `author-year-slug.md` (e.g., `wei-2022-cot.md`)
- Queries: question as slug (e.g., `does-scale-improve-reasoning.md`)

## Frontmatter

All pages must include YAML frontmatter:

```yaml
---
type: entity | ---> people | concept | source | query | comparison | synthesis | overview
title: 使用中文
tags: []
related: []
created: YYYY-MM-DD
updated: YYYY-MM-DD
---
```

issues.title: fix: default the Anthropic preset to claude-sonnet-4-6
issues.body:
hey! tiny one ahead of the sonnet 4.5 retirement.

`claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929` is deprecated and retires on the Claude API on november 30, 2026 ([model deprecations](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/model-deprecations)). the Anthropic preset uses it as `defaultModel`, and `preset-resolver` falls back to that whenever there's no model override, so new Anthropic setups would start on a model that stops working in a couple of weeks.

what changed:

* `src/components/settings/llm-presets.ts`: the Anthropic preset's `defaultModel` is now `claude-sonnet-4-6`, same as the Claude Code CLI preset

i left `suggestedModels` alone. side note though: that list still has a few ids that are already retired (`claude-sonnet-4-20250514`, `claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022`, `claude-3-5-haiku-20241022`), happy to prune those in a follow up if you want.

what i ran:

* `npm run typecheck` (`tsc --build`): passes
* `npx vitest run` on `preset-resolver.test.ts`, both `llm-providers.test.ts` files and `reasoning-capabilities.test.ts`: 4 files, 143 tests passed

went with 4.6 as the closest drop in. the deprecations page lists `claude-sonnet-5-5` as the recommended long term replacement, happy to switch if you'd rather.

issues.title: [Bug] MinerU cloud connection fails with HTTP 403 “Invalid CORS request” on Windows
issues.body:
## Description

Testing the MinerU cloud connection in LLM Wiki 0.6.13 on Windows fails with:

```text
测试失败: HTTP 403: Invalid CORS request
```

Disabling VPN and the application's proxy does not resolve the issue.

## Environment

- OS: Windows
- LLM Wiki: 0.6.13
- HTTP plugin: tauri-plugin-http 2.5.9
- MinerU backend: Cloud (`mineru.net`)
- WebView origin: `http://tauri.localhost`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open Settings → MinerU PDF Parser.
2. Enable MinerU and select the cloud backend.
3. Enter a MinerU API token.
4. Click “Test Connection”.

**Expected:** The connection test succeeds.

**Actual:** The application reports `HTTP 403: Invalid CORS request`.

## Investigation

The installed application's native Tauri HTTP plugin was tested against a local HTTP capture endpoint. It automatically added:

```http
Origin: http://tauri.localhost
User-Agent: tauri-plugin-http/2.5.9
```

Requests were then sent through the same installed plugin to:

```text
POST https://mineru.net/api/v4/extract/task
```

Using the same saved API token and an empty JSON body (`{}`), changing only the Origin handling produced:

| Origin handling | Response |
| --- | --- |
| Default plugin behavior | HTTP 403: `Invalid CORS request` |
| Explicitly set `Origin: ""` | HTTP 200: `{"code":-10002,"msg":"field \"url\" is not set"}` |

The empty body was intentional to avoid creating parsing tasks during diagnosis. Removing Origin allowed the request to reach API parameter validation.

## Root cause

`testMineruConnection()` already uses the native HTTP plugin through `getHttpFetch()`, so this is not simply a browser-fetch CORS issue.

In tauri-plugin-http 2.5.9, the native implementation adds the WebView's origin when no Origin header is supplied. MinerU rejects `http://tauri.localhost`.

The plugin supports removing the header when `Origin` is explicitly set to an empty string and the `unsafe-headers` feature is enabled. LLM Wiki 0.6.13 already enables this feature.

Relevant sources:

- [MinerU request implementation](https://github.com/nashsu/llm_wiki/blob/v0.6.13/src/lib/mineru.ts)
- [Tauri HTTP plugin Origin handling](https://github.com/tauri-apps/plugins-workspace/blob/http-v2.5.9/plugins/http/src/commands.rs)
- [Enabled HTTP plugin features](https://github.com/nashsu/llm_wiki/blob/v0.6.13/src-tauri/Cargo.toml)

## Suggested fix

Add an explicit empty Origin header to the cloud-specific `mineruHeaders()` helper:

```diff
 async function mineruHeaders(token: string): Promise<HeadersInit> {
   return {
     "Content-Type": "application/json",
     Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,
+    Origin: "",
   }
 }
```

This keeps the change scoped to MinerU cloud API requests and covers connection testing, task submission, and polling through the shared helper.

Simply omitting or deleting Origin does not help, because the plugin adds it automatically.

## Validation

I applied the equivalent change as a local patch to the installed application's embedded JavaScript bundle.

After the change:

- The application started normally.
- The original `testMineruConnection()` function succeeded using the saved token and MinerU's official demo PDF.
- The application continued to work normally after restarting.

The official demo was used for the connection test; no personal documents were uploaded during verification. The demo's final parsing result and the complete document ingestion workflow were not independently verified.

issues.title: feat(search): add Keenable web search provider (key-free by default)
issues.body:
Adds **Keenable** (https://keenable.ai) as a web search provider in Settings → Web Search, next to Tavily, Brave, Exa and the others. Keenable is an independent web index built for agents.

- `SearchProvider` gains `"keenable"`, with a provider entry in the settings section.
- `hasConfiguredSearchProvider` treats Keenable as ready without a key. With no key it uses the key-free public endpoint (`POST /v1/search/public` with `X-Keenable-Title: LLM Wiki`). A key switches it to `/v1/search` with `X-API-Key`.
- Rust (`agent/tools.rs`): `keenable_request` / `keenable_search`, a dispatch arm, and a unit test for request building.
- Tests: `web-search.test.ts` has a new assertion, and vitest passes. The Rust side is rustfmt-clean, but I couldn't compile the Tauri crate in my sandbox because system libraries are missing, so please let CI confirm.

Docs: https://docs.keenable.ai. Disclosure: I work with the Keenable team.
